title: Is the Last Check-In All You Need? Next POI Recommendation: Recall and Rerank

problem.claim: Next-POI recommendation must predict a user's next point of interest from historical check-ins.

gap.claim: Severe dataset sparsity makes long-range transition modeling difficult to learn reliably, while higher-order transition patterns are often too sparse to exploit.

contributions.claim: K1-POI formulates sparse next-POI prediction as candidate generation followed by calibration.
The recall stage uses a most-recent-check-in-only self-attention backbone with a lightweight contrastive objective to retrieve a top-K candidate set aligned with the ground-truth next POI.
The rerank stage uses an efficient model-agnostic Spatio-Temporal Prior Reranker to reorder top-K candidates using training-split spatio-temporal priors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that K1-POI achieves strong performance across three public datasets.
The authors report that statistics-based guess baselines and analyses explain benchmark performance largely through user preference, one-step transition routines, and spatio-temporal habits.

narrative_sequence.summary: Historical-check-in sparsity makes reliable long-range next-POI transition modeling difficult.
The authors identify last-check-in dominance and rapid sparsity of higher-order transitions.
K1-POI performs recall with a last-check-in-only backbone and reranking with spatio-temporal priors.
Experiments and analyses report strong performance, attribute benchmark behavior to short-range preferences and habits, and question long-range transition mining under sparse benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The last check-in often provides the most predictive signal, while higher-order transitions quickly become too sparse to exploit.

interpretation.claim: Under sparse benchmark settings, a short-horizon model may capture much of the available predictive signal.

application.claim: Evaluate simple recent-history and statistics-based baselines before investing in long-range transition modeling.

exception.claim: This lesson may not transfer to datasets or settings where longer histories are sufficiently dense and informative.

unknowns: The three public datasets are not identified.
No performance metrics, numerical results, or comparison baselines are provided.
The abstract does not specify the exact spatio-temporal priors, model architecture details, or training settings.
